extracted.intended_audience: school and LEA administrators, higher education institutions, policymakers, and public commenters on Title IX rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble discussing public comments on the Department's Regulatory Impact Analysis and implementation burdens of the final Title IX regulations, including data sources, cost estimates, staffing, training, supportive measures, evidence access, and hearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and disclose data limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and account for limitations, underreporting, overreporting, and misreporting in data sources (e.g., Clery Act, CRDC) and do not accept such datasets at face value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters noted underreporting in Clery and CRDC data (AAUW findings, EEOC Task Force example). The Department identified data limitations in the NPRM and requested public input on comprehensive data sources. Where data are limited, explain rationale and coding decisions and be transparent about quality issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify assumptions and provide basis for calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the evidentiary basis for key assumptions used in cost and burden calculations (for example, the assumed percent of incidents resulting in formal complaints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters criticized unclear assumptions (e.g., ‘assumes that only 50 percent of the incidents reported in the CRDC would result in a formal complaint’). The Department must explain how survey data were coded and provide alternative estimates in sensitivity analyses to show impact of assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple data sources and sensitivity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on the best available data while presenting alternative estimates and sensitivity analyses to show how results depend on assumptions and data choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM provided alternative estimates and a Sensitivity Analysis section. Where higher-quality comprehensive data are absent, rely on available sources but present alternatives and make underlying calculations available to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate and cite relevant peer-reviewed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult and reference academic, peer-review research relevant to cost estimates and policy impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenter asked why academic research was not consulted; the Department states it consulted relevant research as cited in the NPRM. Use published studies to inform estimates where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for outliers and aim to capture the overall average
rubrics_metrics.description: When estimating burdens across a universe of recipients, acknowledge outliers but choose assumptions intended to capture the overall average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognized outliers in recipients and used assumptions to capture average impacts, while noting sensitivity to outliers and adjusting assumptions elsewhere to address underestimation concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define recipient units correctly (LEA vs operating component)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify who the recipient is (e.g., LEA as the recipient rather than each individual school) and assign obligations consistent with that definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters worried each school in an LEA would need its own Title IX Coordinator; the Department clarifies final regs do not require each operating component to designate independently and that LEA is the recipient under §106.30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance uniform standards against small-entity burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to apply the same procedural requirements to small entities or create lighter standards, weighing fairness/due process against cost burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One institution suggested lighter requirements for schools with fewer than 3,000 students and fewer than ten complaints; the Department declined, stating students at all schools are entitled to consistent, constitutionally fair grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate realistic time to revise policies and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate time burdens for revising grievance procedures that reflect actual active work hours and the institutional processes for drafting, consulting, and approving policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters estimated two to six months for policy changes; Department revised estimates to specific hours for Title IX Coordinators, attorneys, and administrators at LEA, IHE, and other entities (e.g., LEA: 6 hours Title IX Coordinator, 24 hours attorney, 2 hours administrator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow role flexibility to limit unnecessary hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit recipients to assign required roles (Title IX Coordinator, investigator, decision-maker) to existing staff where there is no conflict of interest, to avoid mandatory new hires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations do not preclude the Title IX Coordinator from serving as investigator if no conflict exists; decision-makers may be individuals already serving in decision-making capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate staffing burdens conservatively and ground salary estimates in labor data
rubrics_metrics.description: When projecting staffing costs, use realistic wage-rate data and consider the likelihood and magnitude of hiring responses by recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commenter estimated $400,000 on salary; Department disagreed and cited BLS wage-rate data estimating that hiring a full-time Title IX Coordinator, investigator, and decision-maker would cost less than $325,000 on average and that annual hour burden across the three roles would be less than 400 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include training costs and account for turnover
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate duration and frequency of training for Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and persons facilitating informal resolution; include retraining or training for a portion of personnel annually to account for turnover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department increased training estimates from 4 to 8 hours per staff member and added training for 50% of personnel each year to account for turnover or onboarding additional staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow remote/virtual training to reduce burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Training need not be in-person; recipients may conduct training online or virtually to mitigate travel/time burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department notes final regulations do not require in-person training and do not preclude online/virtual training; LEAs likely can incorporate Title IX training into existing training offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train persons designated to facilitate informal resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must train any person they designate to facilitate an informal resolution process about their role and execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requires training of persons designated by the recipient to facilitate informal resolution; Department adjusted cost estimates to include such training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate costs of supportive measures and perform sensitivity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Include per-instance costs for supportive measures in cost estimates and run alternative models to assess sensitivity (e.g., $100, $250, $1000 scenarios).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department added an average cost of $250 per provision of supportive measures, acknowledged this may over- or under-estimate actual costs, and presented alternative models to show impact on total estimated costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat supportive measures costs as outcome-independent where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that provision of supportive measures may not be dependent on the outcome of the grievance process and estimate provision costs accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department noted its assumptions regarding supportive measures are not related to case outcomes and asked for public input on costs; many supportive measures (e.g., class changes) may have little to no cost while others (e.g., security escorts) are costlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide parties reasonable access to evidence (electronic or hard copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow recipients discretion to provide evidence in an electronic format or a hard copy for parties to inspect and review; do not mandate specific file-sharing platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed regs had caused confusion about file-sharing platform requirements; Department revised §106.45(b)(5)(vi) to permit electronic or hard-copy provision and removed the prescriptive file-sharing reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow recipients discretion on inspection/review timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide parties a meaningful time to inspect/review evidence and respond to investigative reports (ten calendar or business days), but allow recipients discretion whether to use calendar or business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department retained two ten-day periods (inspect/review evidence; respond to investigative report) and said recipients may choose calendar or business days and that adequate time is not itself an undue burden on small entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure access to advisors for cross-examination without mandating attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have access to advisors for cross-examination at live hearings; advisors may be, but need not be, attorneys and are not required to have specialized training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party lacks an advisor at a live hearing, the institution must provide one for the limited purpose of conducting cross-examination; recipients are not required to supply attorneys or specially trained advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate frequency of recipient-provided services realistically
rubrics_metrics.description: When projecting costs for recipient-provided advisors, electronic evidence platforms, or other services, estimate how often recipients will need to provide such services rather than assuming universal or frequent need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department reasoned instances requiring recipient-provided advisors will be minimal and thus unlikely to justify hiring additional highly paid staff solely for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope RIA analyses to practicable and valuable questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit regulatory analyses to questions that can be effectively and efficiently conducted and that would meaningfully inform estimates; decline analyses of unclear value or infeasible scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters requested analyses of impacts on federal background investigations; Department declined, citing uncertainty about feasibility, effectiveness, and how results would be incorporated into estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate economic significance under executive orders and identify deregulatory actions if required
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether final regulations are economically significant under EO 12866 and whether they impose net costs under EO 13771; where required, identify deregulatory actions to offset additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department revised its analysis and determined the final regulations are economically significant and impose net costs; in accordance with EO 13771, the Department will identify two deregulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overbroad retraining requirements when policy distribution suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use policy distribution to notify employees of changes in mandatory-reporting status where appropriate instead of requiring retraining of all employees, when the objective can be accomplished more efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declined to include retraining all staff to ensure they are not 'responsible employees' and suggested policy distribution could achieve the same purpose in many instances.
